title: Interface Learnings: Hazira gas terminal release and fire, 2020
audience: Maintenance and materials management; operations and emergency planning

incident.title: Hazira gas terminal condensate release and fire

data_quality.text: Draft learnings from an unreviewed analysis: the ProbeMatrix investigation status is in progress and no finding is marked as edited by a person. Validate before adoption.
The export mentions regulator involvement but its summary sheet says 'Reportable to Regulator: No'. Confirm the reporting status with the organisation; this pack does not decide it.

FND-44219027 (night-time darkness during the response) carries a reviewer downgrade vote. It appears here only inside an engine-generated table, pasted unchanged; no learning rests on it, as in the register.

bottom_line.text: The seam between Mechanical Maintenance (F02) and Materials Management (F06) carried the release source: 27 findings name both, and they describe one condition, a locally bought O-ring used as the regular substitute for a gasket whose specification was lost.
Neither side owned the part: no role owned the gasket specification, the quality control of its purchase, or the authority to approve a substitute.

That seam sits on the prevention side, at pressure-boundary integrity. On the mitigation side, the seam between Operations & Control Room (F01) and Emergency Planning & Command (F09b) carried the isolation decision: 31 findings name both, and the plan gave neither side the criteria or the authority to isolate.

The largest seams by shared findings are Operations & Control Room with Mechanical Maintenance (71) and Mechanical Maintenance with Asset Integrity, Corrosion & Inspection (40). Each needs its own joint review.

sections.heading: F02 Mechanical Maintenance and F06 Materials Management

items.text: What passes between them is a part: the seal for the retaining plate of the 1986 condensate meter. Stores and procurement buy and issue it; maintenance fits it to a flange machined for a rectangular-slot gasket [FND-6B3A6492; EVD-8645; EVD-0064].

items.group: What went wrong at the seam
items.text: An ownership gap. The original gasket specification was not on file and no role owned re-establishing it, so locally bought round O-rings were purchased with no specification or quality check and fitted as a regular practice [FND-A0017E28; FND-B56701CA; FND-23139BF9; EVD-8645]. The switch was never recorded as a management-of-change decision [FND-5A5F6AB3; EVD-2986], and the job of 18 September 2020 was manned with no independent quality check of the part [FND-615DB819; EVD-2894].

With no recorded authority and a flat authority gradient, staff at the working level made the substitution, and the practice was authorised without being reviewed against a specification [FND-2CEE8915; FND-42BEF461]. Each side could reasonably take the part as settled: stores supplied what the job used, and the job used what stores supplied. Three replacements in 22 months did not prompt a review [FND-AC9A1E69; EVD-1494].

items.lesson: A pressure-boundary seal fitted without a written specification is an unreviewed change, however routine the substitute has become.
items.explanation: Maintenance fitted locally bought O-rings to a rectangular-slot flange across three replacements, with no specification, quality check or recorded authority [FND-7A32AC87; FND-852B7EC7; EVD-8645].

items.lesson: Buying a substitute for a pressure part without a specification moves an engineering decision to the purchase order.
items.explanation: The acquisition process supplied an unspecified round O-ring for a flange machined for a rectangular-slot gasket, with no specification or quality control [FND-6B3A6492; FND-A0017E28; EVD-8645].

items.change: Re-establish the meter seal specification (manufacturer data or an engineered equivalent), hold it as a controlled item, and have stores issue pressure-boundary seals only against that specification reference. A substitute part needs an approved change record before it is issued.
items.indicator: Share of pressure-boundary seals issued from stores with a specification reference and a certificate, visible to both stores and maintenance.

sections.heading: F01 Operations & Control Room and F09b Emergency Planning & Command

items.text: What passes between them is a decision: whether, when and by whom the plant is isolated in a major release. Emergency planning writes it into the on-site disaster management plan; the control room and the shift in-charges have to take it on the night [FND-500E0B2D; FND-82761CC5; EVD-4052; EVD-3932].

items.group: What went wrong at the seam
items.text: Authority with neither side. The plan named hydrocarbon leakage but gave no isolation or stoppage criteria [FND-446A7956; EVD-4052], isolation authority was not allocated to the on-shift operators [FND-8DAFDADC; EVD-7340], and the isolation intent was never passed to the night shift through the plan or standing orders [FND-BB4CC662]. The decision went up the chain by phone, and the first isolation valve was closed 46 minutes after the leak was first detected [FND-36179046; FND-AEA16F83; EVD-6414].

The major-leak scenario was formally identified in the plan, but its isolation criteria were never defined and the risk of leaving them out was never assessed [FND-33D32D4C; FND-6472CD15]. Each side could reasonably take the decision as covered: the plan named the scenario, and the shift followed the escalation chain it knew [FND-D1DF4895; EVD-3932].

items.lesson: An emergency plan that names a release scenario but not who may isolate, and on what criteria, leaves the decision to escalation.
items.explanation: The plan's hydrocarbon-leak guidance omitted isolation and stoppage criteria and delegated authority [FND-730D0DCA; FND-5C7B163D; EVD-4052].

items.lesson: When a release blocks access to the source, the shift's task changes from finding the leak to isolating from a distance, and it needs the authority to do so at once.
items.explanation: Dense vapour stopped anyone approaching the source, while the isolation decision waited on senior staff who were called at about 02:35 [FND-BDD73BA2; FND-4245FBF2; EVD-9612].

items.change: Write isolation and stoppage criteria, the isolation valve list and delegated authority down to control-room shift level into the plan, as one jointly owned section, and test it in unannounced night-shift drills without senior staff present.
items.indicator: Time from confirmed release to the isolation decision in night-shift drills, recorded in the drill record both sides read.
items.why_not_stronger: The stronger control, remote isolation of the gas terminal valves (LR-09), needs these criteria and this authority to be used without waiting for escalation; the two go together.

lint_ok.reason: the written criteria and delegated authority are the system fix for the plan (L4); the engineering control they pair with is the remote isolation of LR-09

sections.intro: One line per seam in the matrix. Each pair reviews the record named.

F02 and F07: maintenance and the engineering authority review changes made through work orders against the MOC log.
F02 and F08: maintenance supervisors and planners review open notifications on equipment back in service.
F01 and F09b: control-room leads and emergency planners review the plan's isolation criteria against the drill records.
F01 and F13: shift in-charges and plant leadership review who may isolate, on what criteria, at night.
F01 and F04: control-room leads and instrument engineers review what the detection and pressure instruments actually send to the control room.
F01 and F07: operations and engineering review the drawings and the emergency valve design together.
F02 and F11: maintenance and HSE review the permit and job safety plan records for pressure-boundary jobs.

limits: This pack opens two seams: F02 with F06 (the 27 findings both name; the pack's scope) and, on the mitigation side, F01 with F09b (31 findings). The other seams in the matrix need their own sections.
The export does not record who in stores or maintenance decided to use the O-rings, or when the practice began.

gaps.text: When the substitute O-ring practice began, and who first approved it, is not in the export.
gaps.evidence_needed: Purchase and stores issue records for the meter seals since commissioning, and the first work order that used a locally bought O-ring.
